# policy

In [EhOsContract.Contract](contract-dsl.md), section `contract`.

```elixir
policy name, label
```

Whenever an event happens, issue a command.

**Arguments**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Docs |
|------|------|----------|---------|------|
| <a id="contract-policy-name"></a>`name` | `atom` | yes |  | The policy's name. |
| <a id="contract-policy-label"></a>`label` | `String.t` | yes |  | The rule, as the business states it. |

**Options**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Docs |
|------|------|----------|---------|------|
| <a id="contract-policy-handles"></a>`handles` | `atom \| list(atom)` | yes |  | The events it reacts to. |
| <a id="contract-policy-issues"></a>`issues` | `atom \| list(atom)` | yes |  | The commands it may issue. |
| <a id="contract-policy-delivery"></a>`delivery` | `:in_transaction \| :at_least_once` |  |  | When it runs; `:in_transaction` when left out, which a reaction to an event of another context has to state (X10). |
| <a id="contract-policy-idempotency"></a>`idempotency` | `[key: atom, owner: :self \| :downstream \| :infrastructure]` |  |  | What makes a second delivery harmless, and who keeps it so: `[key: :event_id, owner: :self]`. |
| <a id="contract-policy-source"></a>`source` | `String.t` |  |  | Where the policy comes from in the material. |

Inside it: [`constraint`](#contract-policy-constraint).
